title: Reason Code 3: malformed Access-Request (usually a wrong shared secret)
plain_english: NPS received a RADIUS packet it could not parse or verify and discarded it (Event 6274). In practice the packet is rarely malformed: when the shared secret differs between the NAS and the RADIUS client entry on NPS, the Message-Authenticator check fails and NPS reports the packet as malformed. The user's credentials were never looked at.

any: received from the network access server was malformed

causes.cause: Shared secret mismatch between the NAS and the RADIUS Client entry on NPS.
causes.next_check: Re-enter the secret on both sides (NPS console > RADIUS Clients > the client > Shared secret); watch for trailing spaces, quotes copied from a config file, or a secret longer than the NAS supports.

causes.cause: The request arrives from a different IP than the RADIUS Client entry (NAT, secondary interface), so NPS matched a different client entry with a different secret.
causes.next_check: Compare 'Client IP Address' in the event with the NAS's configured source address; on the NAS pin the RADIUS source interface.

causes.cause: Genuinely malformed packet: a truncated UDP fragment or a vendor attribute NPS cannot decode.
causes.next_check: Capture on the NPS server (pktmon or Wireshark) and look at the failing Access-Request: length mismatch or fragmentation points at the network, an odd VSA at the NAS firmware.
